laws-of-motion.overview: Newton's Laws of Motion form the backbone of classical mechanics. Mastering these principles is crucial for cracking mechanics-based questions in the upcoming exams.

formulas.name: Newton's Second Law
formulas.explanation: The rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to the applied force.

formulas.name: Banking of Roads
formulas.explanation: Maximum safe velocity on a banked road with friction.

commonMistakes: Confusing mass with weight (Weight varies with g, Mass is an intrinsic property).
Ignoring the intended direction of friction leading to incorrect free body diagrams (FBDs).
laws-of-motion.pyqAnalysis: Appears 3-4 times per year in JEE Mains and NEET. Focus areas include connected bodies (pulley systems), friction on inclined planes, and circular motion dynamics.

work-energy-and-power.overview: Work, Energy, and Power connect kinematics with dynamics through scalar quantities. Understanding the Work-Energy Theorem offers powerful shortcuts for complex mechanics problems.

formulas.name: Work-Energy Theorem
formulas.explanation: The net work done by all forces on an object equals its change in kinetic energy.

formulas.name: Conservative Force & PE
formulas.explanation: Conservative force is the negative gradient of potential energy.

commonMistakes: Applying the work-energy theorem incorrectly by forgetting to account for non-conservative work (e.g. friction).
Miscalculating power as simply total force times average velocity instead of the dot product of force and instantaneous velocity.
work-energy-and-power.pyqAnalysis: Consistent 2-3 questions per paper. High probability of integration-based variable force problems and vertical circular motion scenarios.
